parts.label: Part 2
parts.article:
Juliet: Great to have you here today, Hamish. I've been a fan of yours for ages. The very first rock concert I went to when I was 13, your band was playing.

Hamish: Gosh, I'd like to thank this station too, Juliet. If I remember rightly, Ray Rogers' interest in Sound Whole's second album put us on the map.

Juliet: Good old Ray, Alas, who could forget when Sound Whole broke up and Ray wept live on his show.

Hamish: But to set the record straight, Sound Whole isn't getting back together despite rumors on social networks. My performing days are over.

Juliet: Even solo?

Hamish: Especially solo. Frankly, solo gigs were a nightmare. I was so anxious every time I went out onto a stage. Live audiences seriously scare me.

Juliet: Yet you've got such a rapport with them. You look so relaxed in those clips on YouTube.

Hamish: Yeah, well. One thing the social networks did get right is the reason I quit performing.

Juliet: Oh.

Hamish: I was manic when I was on the road with the band. Crazy. I'd stay up days on end. Back home, I was horribly depressed. I’d sleep for a week. My life was a mess, my first wife left me. And my second wife left me. I’ve got three children I hardly know. My son sent me a card just before Sound Whole split up. In which he’d written he’d seen more of me on TV than in the flesh.

Juliet: So how long have you been making acoustic guitars, Hamish?

Hamish: Full time for about three years. My sister and I work together. She sources the materials and does the books. I build instruments.

Juliet: I checked on the internet last night and it’s a long process to make a guitar.

Hamish: You bet. There’s at least 15 steps. I won’t go into them all now, but sourcing the wood, the first step is crucial. Cheap guitars use softer wood, which equates with poor sound quality. But harder wood is scarce these days. For instance, the back of a great guitar, historically, was made from Brazilian Rosewood. But the supply is minuscule now. I use East Indian Rosewood, which will also disappear soon. Likewise, Spruce was once preferred for the top of a guitar, but I use Cedar, which is more plentiful.

Juliet: I thought guitars were mainly Mahogany.

Hamish: Cheap guitars, yes. But only the necks of good ones. The neck must resist distortion when pulled by the strings. And it mustn’t swell or contract with changes in temperature and humidity. Mahogany’s perfect for the neck.

Juliet: I like that wavy pattern you get on the tops and backs of guitars. How’s that done?

Hamish: That pattern is called book matching. A thick block of wood about half the size of the body is sliced horizontally. The two pieces are laid together with the grain continuous before they’re glued.

Juliet: Right.

Hamish: The next two steps are to see the top of the guitar into that sensual shape and cut out the sound hole.

Juliet: What’s inside the guitar to control its vibration and improve its tone?

Hamish: Braces. Narrow little bits of wood, glued in an X pattern. The process is known as strutting. The back also has strutting to reflect sound waves.

Juliet: Interesting. How's the neck made?

Hamish: It's carved from a single piece of Mahogany, and a metal rod is driven up into it for reinforcement.

Juliet: How'd you get those lovely curved sides?

Hamish: Strips are cut, sanded and soaked in water. They're moulded until they're set in that shape. When everything's been glued together, the back, the sides, the top and the neck, the guitar is put into clamps for several days. There are some other reinforcements too, like end blocks and bindings.

Juliet: I guess precision is the key to much of this work.

Hamish: Absolutely. In fact, guitar making has improved my mental health because everything's nice and slow and precise. I'm alone in my workshop dealing with wood. It has a calming effect.

Juliet: It seems as though you sound whole again.

Hamish: Please. No more silly puns in the name of our band. I spent 14 years explaining that Whole was spelt with a W.

questions.question: Paying a visit to a rock concert as a teenager

analyses.content: Juliet 提到她在 13 岁（即 teenager）时去看的第一个摇滚音乐会就是 Hamish 乐队的演出。
The very first rock concert I went to when I was 13, your band was playing.
不要因为 Hamish 是音乐家就选 A，题目问的是谁“作为青少年去看了演唱会”，Hamish 是台上表演的人。
Alas, who could forget when Sound Whole broke up and Ray wept live on his show.
Wept 是 cry 的文学说法。虽然 Hamish 是乐队成员，但哭的是粉丝兼主持人 Ray。
Juliet 回忆说，当 Sound Whole 乐队解散时，节目主持人 Ray 在他的直播节目中 wept（哭泣，即 crying）。

questions.question: Very nervous about performing in public

analyses.content: Frankly, solo gigs were a nightmare. I was so anxious every time I went out onto a stage. Live audiences seriously scare me.
Juliet 说他在视频里看起来很放松（relaxed），但这只是干扰信息，Hamish 紧接着就反驳说那是假象，他其实吓坏了。
Hamish 坦白说个人独奏对他来说是噩梦，每次上台他都非常 anxious（焦虑）和害怕。
My life was a mess, my first wife left me. And my second wife left me. ...Work adversely affected private life.
不要选 Ray，虽然他也哭了，但那是因为乐队解散，并没有提到他的私生活受影响。
Hamish 描述他的私生活一团糟（life was a mess），两任妻子离开了他，孩子也和他不亲，这都是工作导致的负面影响。

groups.contentHtml:
Stage 1:
• Mahogany is used for the neck as it can endure changes in and humidity.
Stage 2:
• Braces are glued onto the top and back to improve and reflect sound waves.
Stage 3:
• Wet wooden strips are placed into a curved mold.
Stage 4:
• The neck is carved from a single piece of wood, and a metal rod is driven into it for .
Stage 5:
• The back, sides, top, and neck are glued and clamped together for .

analyses.content: And it mustn’t swell or contract with changes in temperature and humidity.
题目中已有 "and humidity"，只需填并列的名词 temperature。
Hamish 解释说琴颈（neck）必须不能随 temperature（温度）和湿度的变化而膨胀或收缩。
Juliet 问吉他内部有什么装置可以控制振动并改善 tone（音色/音调），Hamish 回答是 Braces。
What’s inside the guitar to control its vibration and improve its tone?
注意题目问的是 Braces 的作用（improve...），答案就在问题本身包含的信息里。
It's carved from a single piece of Mahogany, and a metal rod is driven up into it for reinforcement.
听到 "metal rod" 后要紧抓 "for" 后面的目的名词。
琴颈是用整块桃花心木雕刻的，并且植入一根金属杆用于 reinforcement（加固）。
...the guitar is put into clamps for several days.
题目问的是时长，不要漏掉 quantity word "several"。
所有部件胶合后，吉他会被放入夹具中固定 several days（几天）。

questions.question: Why does Hamish enjoy making guitars?

analyses.content: In fact, guitar making has improved my mental health because everything's nice and slow and precise. ... It has a calming effect.
虽然 A 选项提到仔细的木工活（precise work），但这只是过程，他享受的根本原因是对心理健康的益处。
Hamish 明确表示制作吉他改善了他的 mental health（心理健康），因为它有镇静作用（calming effect）。

questions.question: How is the name of Hamish’s old band spelt?

analyses.content: Please. No more silly puns... I spent 14 years explaining that Whole was spelt with a W.
不要选 C (Sound Hole)，那是吉他上的发声孔，虽然是个双关语（pun），但乐队真名拼写带 W。
Hamish 最后说他花了 14 年解释乐队名字里的 "Whole" 是以 W 开头的（即 Sound Whole，意为“声音完整/健康”）。
